note: The two sets are essentially identical claim-for-claim; the only differences are trivial wording variations in conditions ('science' vs 'science mode'). Both contain the same three defective claims: a readout-rate claim carrying the 60 K temperature value, an IFS field of view misread as 0.38"×0.38" instead of 3.8"×3.8", and a claim whose quote misreads 'planned variant' as 'planar variant' and duplicates the IFS 1k×1k format claim. Both also state the same table facts correctly and both carry the same duplicated bandpass facts (stated once with a bare 'range' entity and once under the channel name).
remarks: Both sets share the same defects: 'IFS detector | readout rate | 60 K' binds a temperature to a readout-rate attribute (the page gives no IFS readout rate, only 'very high frame rates'); the IFS FOV is 3.8"×3.8" per the text, not 0.38"×0.38"; and the quote 'planar variant' is a misread of 'planned variant' and duplicates the other IFS 1k×1k format claim. Both also duplicate the UV 0.2–0.45 and Visible 0.45–1.0 bandpass facts under both a bare 'bandpass | range' entity and the channel name. Important facts both sets miss: CCD201 operated at 153K, CCD readout at 1 kHz during thruster firing, the LMAPD guide detector cooled to 60K, the 32×32 pixel pupil image with 12 cm pixels, and the 20% coronagraph bandwidth / four observations / two coronagraphs statement. Minor formatting noise in both: '3.8"×3.8" "' and '32 pixels pixels' unit duplication.
